chapters.title: The Land
lines: Uganda is a country shaped by water.
More of Lake Victoria lies inside it than in any other nation.
At Jinja, the Nile leaves the lake and runs north to Egypt.
West of the lake, the Rift Valley drops into salt plains.
And on the Congo border, the Ruwenzori carry snow on the equator.

chapters.title: Kingdoms
lines: By the fourteen hundreds, kingdoms ran this land.
Kitara first, then Bunyoro, Buganda, Ankole and Toro.
Their kings were called Omukama, or Kabaka.
Wealth was salt, iron, cattle and banana groves.
Power was measured in the people who owed you allegiance.
The Kabaka's court was a bureaucracy, with chiefs, pages and tax.

chapters.title: The Outsiders
lines: In eighteen forty-four, a trader from Zanzibar reached the Kabaka.
He wanted ivory. He paid in cloth, beads and guns.
Guns changed who could rule.
In eighteen sixty-two, Speke stood at the Nile's source near Jinja.
And in eighteen seventy-seven, the missionaries arrived.

chapters.title: The Protectorate
lines: In eighteen ninety-four, Britain declared a protectorate.
It was announced, not negotiated.
Bunyoro fought for years. Its king, Kabalega, was exiled.
In nineteen oh one, the railway reached the lake.
Cotton followed, and a new economy of cash crops.
The lake was suddenly a day away from the coast.

chapters.title: Independence
chapters.key: A flag, then a long night
lines: On the ninth of October, nineteen sixty-two, Uganda became independent.
Nine years later, the army took power.
Under Amin, hundreds of thousands died, and sixty thousand Asians were expelled.
War followed war, until nineteen eighty-six, when the rebels took Kampala.
In nineteen sixty-six, the army attacked the Kabaka's palace.

chapters.title: Today
lines: What came next was not a miracle. It was forty years of work.
AIDS prevalence fell by two thirds. Primary school became free.
Oil came out of the ground near Lake Albert.
More than forty-five million people live here now.
The median age is about sixteen.
Kampala is still growing, and so is the country.
